sources_considered.why: Primary release evaluations report hallucinations in three leading reasoning models.
A second developer reports hallucinations during testing of its released model family.
The inspected factuality passages emphasize benchmark accuracy, which alone does not distinguish hallucinations from abstentions.
The search result discusses later models and was not used to establish the July 2025 state.

evidence_items.explanation: The release evaluation reports SimpleQA hallucination rates of 51%, 79%, and 44% for o3, o4-mini, and o1, respectively; PersonQA rates are 33%, 48%, and 16%. These are substantial benchmark failure rates across several models, not estimates of everyday usage.

Testing of approximately final Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 models also found hallucinations. The card reports successful mitigation of one specific hallucination pattern elsewhere, but says that mitigation did not completely eliminate it.

unresolved_gaps: These evaluations do not establish a population-wide hallucination rate across all neural systems or ordinary user requests.
